semantic_preflight.canonical_pair_probability_semantics: For every ordered action pair (a, b), canonical inference evaluates HistGradientBoostingClassifier.predict_proba(x(a)-x(b))[:, 1] as P(a outranks b).
semantic_preflight.canonical_action_aggregation: MEAN_PAIRWISE_WIN_PROBABILITY: score(a) = mean over all other actions b of P(a outranks b); the top action is the maximum score with the frozen deterministic tie-break.
semantic_preflight.blocking_reason: Canonical scoring directly averages unthresholded ordered-pair probabilities and contains no binary B-versus-N decision layer that affects action ranking. Therefore p_model(B>N)>0.55 cannot change any canonical mean action score or rank while MEAN_PAIRWISE_WIN_PROBABILITY remains unchanged. In addition, under ordinary binary semantics, increasing the B-win threshold from 0.50 to 0.55 makes B harder—not easier—to declare above N, contrary to the stated target of improving B-versus-N ordering.
